newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine shares take breather, close lower.
newsitem.headline: Philippine shares take breather, close lower.

text.p: Philippine shares took a pause on Friday after three days of steady climb as local players cashed in their gains in a generally sluggish session, brokers said.

"We are still in a consolidation phase," Spencer Yap, a senior analyst at BPI Capital Corp, said. Investors were awaiting second quarter earning results to come in by mid-July before taking new position in the local shares market, he said.
"Investors are still mixed as to what the second quarter results hold," he said. Projections for the blue chips were diverse, leading to some early selldown in select heavyweights.
Among the losers was San Miguel Corp which announced a major restructuring plan on Thursday, but continued wariness over its earnings prospect dampened its shares on Monday.
The composite index was down by a marginal 2.07 points at 2,835.03. The index had had a three-day runup of 28.45 points.
"The market is undecided right now. It's not convinced it's ready to move up in the near future," Rolly Pineda, vice president of Tower Securities, said.
The best strategy, he said, was to concentrate on selected issues which had gone down to attractive levels.

"We have to be very choosy at this point. We should look at companies which have steady earnings and good stories to tell.. But we have very little to choose from," an analyst at Abacus Securities said.
Analysts expected the market to remain sluggish next week due to the dearth of market-moving news and wariness of foreign investors over the Hong Kong handover.
